front: Who delivered the 'I Have a Dream' speech in 1963?
back: Martin Luther King Jr., during the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom

front: What was the opening line of Lincoln's Gettysburg Address (1863)?
back: 'Four score and seven years ago our fathers brought forth on this continent, a new nation, conceived in Liberty'

front: Who said 'We shall fight on the beaches' in 1940?
back: Winston Churchill, addressing the House of Commons after the Dunkirk evacuation

front: What speech did JFK give on January 20, 1961?
back: His inaugural address, famous for 'Ask not what your country can do for you — ask what you can do for your country'

front: Who delivered the 'I Am Prepared to Die' speech in 1964?
back: Nelson Mandela, at the Rivonia Trial in South Africa

front: What did FDR say about fear in his 1933 inaugural address?
back: 'The only thing we have to fear is fear itself'

front: Who gave the 'Tear Down This Wall' speech in 1987?
back: Ronald Reagan, at the Brandenburg Gate in West Berlin

front: What was the Sermon on the Mount?
back: A collection of teachings by Jesus Christ, including the Beatitudes, recorded in the Gospel of Matthew

front: Who said 'Give me liberty, or give me death!' in 1775?
back: Patrick Henry, at the Second Virginia Convention

front: What famous speech did Sojourner Truth deliver in 1851?
back: 'Ain't I a Woman?', at the Women's Convention in Akron, Ohio

front: Who delivered 'The Ballot or the Bullet' speech in 1964?
back: Malcolm X, at Cory Methodist Church in Cleveland, Ohio

front: What was the main message of Emmeline Pankhurst's 'Freedom or Death' speech (1913)?
back: That women's suffrage was worth fighting for, even at the cost of one's life

front: Who gave the 'Blood, Toil, Tears and Sweat' speech in 1940?
back: Winston Churchill, in his first speech as Prime Minister to the House of Commons

front: What did Mahatma Gandhi advocate in his 'Quit India' speech of 1942?
back: The immediate end of British rule in India through nonviolent civil disobedience

front: Who said 'That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind' in 1969?
back: Neil Armstrong, upon stepping onto the Moon's surface

front: What was the main theme of Chief Joseph's 'I Will Fight No More Forever' speech (1877)?
back: The surrender of the Nez Perce tribe after a long retreat, expressing exhaustion and sorrow

front: Who delivered the 'Yes We Can' speech in 2008?
back: Barack Obama, during the New Hampshire primary campaign

front: What famous speech did Queen Elizabeth I give in 1588?
back: The Tilbury Speech, rallying troops against the Spanish Armada: 'I have the body of a weak and feeble woman, but I have the heart and stomach of a king'

front: Who gave the 'Ich bin ein Berliner' speech in 1963?
back: John F. Kennedy, in West Berlin, expressing solidarity with the city's residents

front: What was the key message of Frederick Douglass's 'What to the Slave Is the Fourth of July?' (1852)?
back: That celebrating American freedom was hypocritical while millions remained enslaved

front: Who delivered the 'A Date Which Will Live in Infamy' speech in 1941?
back: Franklin D. Roosevelt, asking Congress to declare war after the attack on Pearl Harbor

front: What speech did Malala Yousafzai give at the United Nations in 2013?
back: A speech advocating for girls' education worldwide, saying 'One child, one teacher, one book, one pen can change the world'

front: Who said 'Mr. Gorbachev, open this gate!' before the more famous line about the wall?
back: Ronald Reagan, in the same 1987 Berlin speech

front: What was Abraham Lincoln's 'House Divided' speech about (1858)?
back: That the nation could not permanently endure half slave and half free

front: Who gave the 'Atoms for Peace' speech in 1953?
back: President Dwight D. Eisenhower, at the United Nations General Assembly

front: What was the significance of Nikita Khrushchev's 'Secret Speech' in 1956?
back: He denounced Stalin's cult of personality and purges before the 20th Congress of the Communist Party

front: Who delivered the 'Rivers of Blood' speech in 1968?
back: Enoch Powell, a controversial British speech opposing mass immigration

front: What speech did Susan B. Anthony give after being arrested for voting in 1873?
back: 'Is It a Crime for a Citizen of the United States to Vote?', arguing the Constitution granted women suffrage

front: Who said 'The lady's not for turning' in 1980?
back: Margaret Thatcher, at the Conservative Party Conference, refusing to reverse her economic policies

front: What was the core message of Vaclav Havel's 'New Year's Address' in 1990?
back: A call for truth, moral renewal, and responsibility as Czechoslovakia transitioned from communism to democracy
